root_cause_label: Third-Party Library Dependency in Test Environment
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent wrote check_cert.py using the third-party `cryptography` library instead of stdlib/subprocess, and although the script ran successfully in the agent's local environment, the automated test harness likely lacked this dependency, causing the test_python_verification_script test to fail.
t_err_evidence: Step 8: Agent creates /app/check_cert.py importing from `cryptography` (x509, default_backend) — a third-party library — instead of using subprocess to call openssl commands or standard ssl module. This is the decisive mistake: the script will fail in any test environment that does not have the cryptography package installed.
t_commit_evidence: Step 10: Agent runs the script locally, sees successful output ('Common Name: dev-internal.company.local', 'Expiration Date: 2026-12-19', 'Certificate verification successful', exit code 0), and considers the task verified. From this point the agent proceeds straight to finish() without reconsidering the dependency assumption.
trigger_explanation: The agent lacked awareness that the test evaluation environment would not have the `cryptography` library available, and did not know (or consider) that the task required a self-contained solution using only stdlib/subprocess. The agent installed cryptography via pip in step 9 to satisfy its own local run, but this installation does not persist to the clean test environment.
forewarning_evidence: Step 8 LLM analysis explicitly flags: 'The script relies on the cryptography library, which may not be available in the environment, causing the test to fail. A robust approach is to use OpenSSL via subprocess...' — this warning was noted in the step annotation but the agent itself did not act on this concern (step 9 just installs the library rather than rewriting to avoid the dependency).
